objections.objection: Switching platforms means re-migrating an existing list and rebuilding sending workflows, which isn't worth the hassle unless something is actually broken.
objections.answer: Buttondown migrates an existing list for free no matter how large it is, which removes the list-size part of the switching-cost objection, though it doesn't speak to rebuilding templates or automations elsewhere.

provenance.quote: This long weekend I fulfilled a long-standing promise to myself to switch my RSS-to-email provider from Mailchimp to Buttondown...

objections.objection: The 'free' plan looks like a loss-leader — tagging, analytics, automations, comments, RSS support and attachments are all separate paid add-ons, so the real cost for anyone who wants a fully-featured newsletter is much higher than 'free'.
objections.answer: One customer called the free plan generous, but that's a single subjective impression with no stated limits or figures; nothing in the evidence addresses what the bill looks like once several named add-ons are stacked on top of the free base.

objections.objection: A support team of four people can't realistically keep up once I'm not the only one emailing them, especially outside their stated 6am–6pm ET hours.
objections.answer: In one documented case, a reported security vulnerability was acknowledged and fixed in under two hours on a Friday night — faster than the stated hours would suggest — but that is one incident, not a stated SLA for support generally.

objections.objection: Newsletter platforms often take a cut of subscription or sponsorship revenue, so running paid content through yet another one risks losing margin that can't be recovered.
objections.answer: Buttondown takes no cut of sponsorships and doesn't charge extra for paid subscribers; creators keep 100% of sponsorship and paid-subscription revenue minus only Stripe's processing fee.

objections.objection: No official SDK or MCP server means generating a client or wrapper before automating anything, which is extra work compared to tools that hand over a ready-made SDK.
objections.answer: Buttondown deliberately skips SDKs and an MCP server in favor of maintaining an OpenAPI spec that any caller can generate a typed client from — a stated trade-off, not a resolved gap, so the integration work still falls on the developer.

objections.objection: Pricing scales with subscriber count, so growing the list this product is supposed to help grow also raises the bill — right when margins on a creator income are thinnest.
